title: Life is poker, not chess
heading: Life is poker, not chess
coreClaim: The chapter argues that life works more like poker than chess because hidden information and luck remain active after choices are made, which means decision quality cannot be read straight off the outcome.
distinctMechanism: The poker-versus-chess contrast explains why certainty hunger and hindsight judgment distort decision-making in real environments.
requiredAnchors: Poker versus chess as the governing contrast.
A good decision can lose and a bad decision can win in a probabilistic setting.
Saying 'I'm not sure' as an honest response to incomplete information.
specificApplications: Judge choices from the live information set.
Use calibrated confidence in forecasts and disagreements.
Keep process accountability even when luck is active.
hardEdgeRequirement: Preserve the tension between incomplete knowledge and committed action.
thresholdQuestion: How do you commit strongly without pretending the board is complete?
